– the failing test (signature + snippet),

– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testNestedDOM` calls `doTest("nested", DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM, "foo;bar; baz ")` which expects to retrieve a string "foo;bar; baz " including trailing spaces, from the XML via JXPath. The test implementation calls `JXPathContext.getValue(xpath)` on path `test/text[@id='nested']` and asserts the string returned matches the expected "foo;bar; baz " including the trailing space.

The bug report states that JXPath trims leading and trailing spaces from values extracted from XML nodes, so ` <value> 12324 56</value>` becomes "12324 56" instead of " 12324 56". This indicates that JXPath's string extraction logic is removing whitespace unintentionally.

The `DocumentContainer` is initialized with the XML resource and model type "DOM", indicating the XML is represented by DOM nodes. The `JXPathContext.getValue(String)` ultimately calls `getValue(xpath, expression)` in `JXPathContextReferenceImpl`, which handles XPath evaluation and value extraction.

The key issue is likely that the extraction of string values from the DOM nodes in JXPath performs a trim operation or uses a method that inherently trims the text content. JXPath should preserve leading and trailing spaces as present in XML element text contents, but currently, it returns values with spaces stripped.

No recent bug reports are related, so the issue is isolated to how string values are extracted from XML DOM nodes when JXPath evaluates XPath expressions.

The root cause is that the method responsible for extracting string values from XML nodes is automatically trimming spaces instead of preserving them. This behavior conflicts with XML text node semantics where spaces should be preserved unless xml:space="preserve" or defaulted accordingly. Because the test expects spaces to be preserved but they are trimmed, the bug lies in how JXPath extracts and returns string values from XML DOM nodes.

Recommended next steps would be to examine the method(s) in JXPath responsible for extracting string values from XML DOM nodes, looking for implicit or explicit trimming calls or conversions that remove spaces. Fixing that logic to preserve leading/trailing spaces will resolve the test failure and match the expected behavior stated in the bug report.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
